text:
Cropping has established precedent, but distinct methods support different interpretations. [Tan et al. (2016)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.08117) train recurrent recommenders on every session prefix paired with its immediately following item; this varies prediction endpoints while retaining each prefix’s original beginning. [CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/html/2010.14395) randomly selects contiguous subsequences as contrastive views alongside next-item prediction. Neither directly establishes the benefit of deleting older context while retaining aligned suffix supervision in GRU4Rec.

[Recency Dropout](https://arxiv.org/html/2201.11016) provides recurrent-specific augmentation evidence, but removes recent activities to encourage dependence on older interests—the opposite direction from dropping an old prefix. Its results therefore support augmentation broadly, rather than a claim that prefix removal improves long-term modeling.

Methodological inference: cropping input x[s:t] and pairing retained positions with their original next-item labels preserves temporal target alignment. It does not make training context match full-history inference: recurrent states start with less context during cropped training. Any gain could reflect regularization, increased emphasis on recent transitions, or altered supervision weighting. A useful control compares stochastic prefix removal against deterministic recent-history truncation with matched target positions, loss normalization, and training updates. Evaluate each trained model separately with full history and the corresponding truncated context. Improvement persisting under full-history inference supports an augmentation benefit; it does not by itself demonstrate that train–inference context mismatch was eliminated.
